newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sappi expects improved 1997 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Sappi expects improved 1997 earnings.

text.p: South African pulp and paper producer Sappi Ltd said on Tuesday it expected earnings for the next financial year to improve amid a positive outlook for the world economy.
"We expect 1997 to be a positive year for the world economy and this should have generally positive outlook oin paper markets and prices," Sappi said.

Earlier Sappi said net income in the year to September 30 1996 was 404 million rand, down sharply from 1.36 billion rand in the previous year. Pretax profit slumped to 531 million rand from 1.68 billion.

The company said it anticipated a slow improvement in the prices of most products from a current low base although new coated paper capacity scheduled in Europe for the end of 1997 could disrupt markets, depressing prices.
It said all its South African mills were beginning to "settle down" and were therefore well equipped to benefit from any upturn in the market.

The adverse effect of the decision to cover forward one third of the group's southern African export sales was complete and the company stood to benefit substantially from the weaker rand in the new year.
"Earnings for the next financial year are therefore expected to improve," Sappi said.
